references.text: This chapter contains the full blessings and curses that Deuteronomy 30:1 refers to, where God sets forth the consequences of obedience and disobedience.
Describes the consequences of the curse and how the Lord will drive the people away to other nations, as mentioned in Deuteronomy 30:1.
Speaks of the people confessing their sins in the lands where they are scattered, and that God will remember His covenant—parallel to the promise of repentance in exile.
Solomon's prayer at the temple dedication anticipates exile and repentance, where the people turn back in their hearts while in captivity, as Deuteronomy 30:1 describes.
Nehemiah reminds God of the promise in Deuteronomy that even if the people are scattered, God will gather them again if they repent.
Daniel reflects on the curses that have come upon Israel and prays for God's grace, in line with the promise of restoration after repentance.
Ephraim repents in exile and longs to return to God, fulfilling the pattern from Deuteronomy 30:1 of taking it to heart among the nations.
Ezekiel prophesies about a remnant that will remember the Lord among the nations where they are scattered and mourn over their sins.
